rows.label: P2 · the vow · new
rows.note: Every promise and non-promise kept. Writer a's draft, the only one Pangram passed: 100% Human (102), try 1; the two closer to the guide's lists were 100% AI.

rows.label: P2 · PROPOSAL · why it only promises what you can keep
rows.text: > "I know you're in there. I love you. You don't have to love me back or trust me yet. I can't promise that nothing painful will happen. Or that I'll always know what to do, or never react badly. But I can promise to tell you the truth and listen when you're angry. I'll make our life together safer where I can, and take the next step I can see to protect you. When I fail, I'll come back to make it right. You don't have to believe these words. Watch what I do." The vow only promises what you can keep, so, unlike with those grown-ups, your little one can actually watch you keep it.
rows.note: Not installed. A line after the vow, from the reviews' good-to-great line. 100% Human (125), try 1.

rows.label: P3 · new
rows.article: Only say the "I love you" part
guide: Use “I love you” only when it is honest.
rows.note: Writer b's, with the wish quoted (no cold read could find it), "on purpose" (an open-ended no-cruelty promise would break soon), "if you can mean that one", and the parenthesis about "love me back". The section is its Pangram test.

rows.label: P3 · PROPOSAL · why the "I love you" has to be meant
rows.text: Only say the "I love you" part if you mean it. Later in the vow you promise to tell your little one the truth, so an "I love you" you don't mean would make that promise false before you've even made it. If you don't mean it, say the goodwill wish from earlier instead ("May you be loving, peaceful, and free"), if you can mean that one, and don't pretend it's the same thing. Or even just promise your little one you won't be cruel to them on purpose. (Then drop the "love me back" part too, but keep "you don't have to trust me yet.")
rows.proposal_of: Only say the "I love you" part

rows.label: P4 · new
rows.article: Whichever you choose, your little one may still answer
rows.note: Your "Big fuckity whoopty doo" for the guide's "Big whoop". The Not Every Hero examples are a bare pointer: Love Doesn't Wait P13 had just used the same two. 100% Human alone (before one repeat was cut), try 1.

rows.label: P4 · PROPOSAL · why small
rows.text: Whichever you choose, your little one may still answer with "Big fuckity whoopty doo." That's allowed, and one beautiful session wouldn't convince me either. Pick one thing to do that's small enough to repeat. A big gesture you later drop would only prove them right to doubt you, but a small thing you keep doing can change their mind. Maybe it's one you already tried in "Not Every Hero Wears A Cape," or just keeping an appointment, eating, or going to bed.

rows.label: P5 · new · ends the section
rows.article: Whenever your little one shows up
guide: You take the adult position again whenever the child appears.
rows.note: Cut: the guide's "rather than one beautiful session", already in P4. The last line calls back your bedtime story. The section with it: 100% Human (326), try 1.

rows.label: P5 · PROPOSAL · you're in your mom's seat now
rows.text: Whenever your little one shows up, you go back to being their grown-up, and you're kind to them while you do it. Sometimes they show up as the one who doesn't want to go to bed. Now you're in my mom's place: you still go to bed, and staying kind about it shows them bedtime isn't a lack of love.
